The majority of acetabular components in this cohort were stable despite achieving a small contact surface between the component and pelvic bone. While three patients experienced migration out of acceptable limits that predict later loosening in primary Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA), it is unclear whether these limits apply specifically to osteoporotic patients. We continue to use cup-cage reconstruction with oversized cups routinely for this indication, but we are exploring the addition of screw fixation to improve stability and reduce loosening.

In conclusion, while the current evidence does not conclusively establish that cup-cage reconstruction with oversized cups provides initial stability in THA for osteoporotic acetabular fractures, it appears to be a viable option for some patients. Further research is needed to fully understand its efficacy and long-term outcomes.
